theorem_title: Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity for the semi-magic counting function
formal_statement:
namespace MagicSquares

theorem semi_magic_reciprocity (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (p : Polynomial ℚ)
    (hp : ∀ t : ℕ, p.eval (t : ℚ) = (semiMagicCount n t : ℚ)) :
    ∀ t : ℤ, p.eval (((-(n : ℤ) - t : ℤ) : ℚ))
      = (-1 : ℚ) ^ (n - 1) * p.eval ((t : ℤ) : ℚ) := by
  sorry

end MagicSquares
natural_language_statement: **The reciprocity law.** Let $n\ge 1$ and let $p\in\mathbb{Q}[X]$ agree with $H_{n}$ on the nonnegative integers. Then $p(-n-t)=(-1)^{n-1}p(t)$ for every integer $t$. This is the reflection $t\mapsto -n-t$ of the lattice-point count, rescaled by the sign $(-1)^{n-1}$; its right-hand side counts the interior of the corresponding polytope, by the Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity law. The identity is not visible from the combinatorial definition of $H_{n}$, which is stated only for nonnegative $t$.

readback.readback:
Let $n$ be a natural number with $1\le n$, and let $p\in\mathbb{Q}[X]$ be any polynomial satisfying that for every natural number $t$, $p(t)=\operatorname{semiMagicCount}(n,t)$ (both sides viewed in $\mathbb{Q}$). Then for every integer $t$,

$$p((-n)-t)=(-1)^{\,n-1}\cdot p(t),$$

where $(-n)-t$ denotes $-n$ minus $t$ (i.e. the integer $-(n+t)$, with $n$ first coerced to $\mathbb{Z}$ and negated, then subtracting $t$, and finally lifted to $\mathbb{Q}$), and the exponent $n-1$ is the natural-number subtraction (safe because $1\le n$). The base $(-1)$ is the rational number $-1$ raised to the natural power $n-1$. Thus the theorem asserts a symmetry of $p$ under the reflection $t\mapsto -n-t$, rescaled by the factor $(-1)^{n-1}$.
